newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice meeting on bankcards said postponed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice meeting on bankcards said postponed.

text.p: A meeting tentatively set between Justice Department officials and representatives of Visa and Mastercard has been postponed, someone familiar with the talks said Tuesday.
The meeting had been set for later in the day.
The Justice Department has been investigating whether Visa and MasterCard have violated antitrust laws by barring their member banks from also issuing American Express Co cards.

The meeting will now take place in coming weeks. At that time the acting assistant attorney general of the antitrust division, Joel Klein, will hear both sides of the debate, those familiar with the issue said.

On one side will be Justice Department staff attorneys, who believe the bankcard companies to be in violation of antitrust laws. On the other side will be attorneys for the bankcard companies, who believe their actions are legal.

The meeting postponement was hinted at last week. The executive vice president and general counsel of Visa, Paul Allen, told Reuters Friday that he believed the Justice Department probe would not be over before April.
